evaluations.evidence: entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Specifies user need to provide identifying metadata; does not prescribe concrete UI widget or internal technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete technical mechanism (sharing a URL) instead of stating the stakeholder need to invite others.

evaluations.evidence: in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete UI widget (single multi-line text field) rather than the underlying need to provide the item to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: States a stakeholder need (visibility of items) without prescribing UI widgets or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user's intent to choose an item; does not mandate a specific UI control or technical solution.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to add items; no concrete UI widget or implementation mechanism is prescribed.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the stakeholder need to modify items; does not force a particular solution.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: States the need to remove items; no UI widget or technical mechanism is imposed.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired behavior/outcome (reveal estimates) without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete algorithmic solution (use the average) rather than the broader need for a way to accept a consensus estimate.

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes an automatic UI behavior/implementation rule instead of stating the underlying need to streamline acceptance when consensus exists.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user's action/need to record the agreed estimate without prescribing how the UI must be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need to re-estimate without prescribing UI or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete data-transfer mechanism/format (spreadsheet) rather than the need to bulk-add stories generally.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific user interaction and data source (copy/paste from spreadsheet) instead of the general need to get stories in quickly.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to find past games without mandating UI controls or technical details.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to see a transcript; does not constrain file formats or UI widgets.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete storage/export format (HTML) which is an implementation choice rather than the general need to save transcripts.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific export format (CSV), an implementation detail instead of the stakeholder need to further process data.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: States the need to remove stored data (delete game); does not prescribe technical means.

evaluations.evidence: entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Lists required account information (user need to provide identity/authentication data) without prescribing specific UI widgets or internal mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Describes the authentication need; although it names credentials, it does not mandate implementation details like protocols or UI widgets.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the need to update account info without prescribing UI or technical solutions.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: States the need to remove user data; not prescribing implementation.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a presentation requirement (local timezone) without mandating particular technical approaches.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete delivery mechanism (email) for password reminders rather than the stakeholder need to recover access.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Specifies user-configurable options (choice of scales) rather than a low-level UI widget or internal algorithm; this captures desired functionality.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: States a capacity constraint/need; not prescribing how invitations are implemented.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete mechanism (receiving a URL and entering name on that page) rather than the general need to join a game.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user's need to view the item under discussion without prescribing UI widgets or technical details.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: States a visibility need for items; no concrete solution imposed.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the informational need (who has estimated) without prescribing UI widgets or mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired timing/behavior for showing estimates, not a low-level implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Specifies interaction timing (when changes are allowed) rather than prescribing UI controls or internal mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes an informational need (view prior estimates) without mandating implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: States the requirement to identify contributions during a round; no concrete solution is prescribed.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a functional feature (shared countdown) and its duration; not a low-level UI widget or technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Describes automatic behavior with respect to a feature's state; it expresses a requirement rather than prescribing internal implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: States the need to navigate historical data without prescribing UI widgets or storage formats.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a consistency requirement for card ordering, not a concrete UI control or implementation mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Describes allowed user interactions based on draw state; no specific UI or technical solution is mandated.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific UI element (thumbnail photo positioned near cards), which is a concrete UI design choice.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Specifies compliance with particular technical standards (XHTML/CSS), which are implementation-level constraints.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Requests a content/resource (definitions) to aid understanding; not a technical implementation or UI widget prescription.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete internal implementation detail (database indexes) rather than the need for acceptable query performance.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes support for specific browser versions (implementation/platform constraint) instead of the general compatibility/accessibility need.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Specifies adherence to a particular technical standard/guideline (W3C accessibility), which is an implementation-level requirement.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: States a non-functional user need (performance/responsiveness) without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the user's need to use any language; though it names Unicode, this is a user-facing capability rather than prescribing internal formats.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Describes a user-perceived quality (URL clarity/predictability) rather than mandating a specific technical solution.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a user-facing quality (helpful error pages) rather than internal implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific storage/privacy mechanism (non-identifiable storage) which constrains implementation choices; this is a storage-level requirement.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need to view usage metrics without prescribing technical formats or specific implementation mechanisms.
